questions.q: Why is "the database feels slow" not a diagnosis, per this lesson?
options: It doesn't tell you whether the cause is one query, one user, the whole server, or storage running out — it's a symptom, not a finding
It always means storage is full
It always means the server needs a restart
It is always caused by a missing index
questions.explain: The checklist in this lesson exists specifically to turn that vague report into a specific, actionable finding.

questions.q: What is the checklist order this lesson recommends, and why does it start where it does?
options: Sessions/connections → CPU → memory → I/O → storage — sessions first because it's the fastest signal and often finds the cause immediately
Storage → memory → CPU → sessions — storage first because it's always the root cause
The order doesn't matter at all, per this lesson
Alphabetical order by DMV name
questions.explain: Checking things out of order wastes time chasing symptoms instead of causes; sessions surface the fastest, most direct signal.

questions.q: Why does storage come last in the checklist, even though a nearly-full database is a real problem?
options: Storage usage changes slowly and rarely explains a sudden "feels slow right now" report, even though it can degrade performance well before actually running out
Storage is never actually relevant to performance
Storage can only be checked once per week
Storage always resolves itself automatically in Azure SQL
questions.explain: This lesson is explicit that storage's slow-moving nature makes it an unlikely explanation for a sudden slowdown, even though it matters.

questions.q: What does a populated (non-zero) blocking_session_id column in sys.dm_exec_requests tell you?
options: That the session in question is being blocked by another specific session — often the entire answer to a slowdown investigation by itself
That the session has been permanently disconnected
That the database has run out of storage
That Extended Events is not running
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_requests shows currently executing requests, and a populated blocking_session_id directly identifies a blocking chain.

questions.q: What comes immediately after Chapter 7 in this course, and why is it sized the way it is?
options: Chapter 8, Query Performance Tuning — the course's single largest chapter at 9 lessons, because query performance is where a DBA spends the most real-world time
Chapter 14, High Availability & Disaster Recovery
The course ends after Chapter 7
Chapter 1, Azure SQL & DBA Foundations, repeated as a review
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly closes Chapter 7 and previews Chapter 8 as the course's largest chapter, covering execution plans, indexes, Query Store, and more.
